te: The Ombudsman points out legal gaps on "venues similar to entertainment venues" after the Lat Phrao beer-house fire
se: A representative of the Office of the Ombudsman explained that the law has no definition and no specific licence for businesses that operate like entertainment venues, which limits safety supervision. The meeting therefore invited the Department of Provincial Administration and the Department of Local Administration to clarify next time. Another complaint was closed because it is before the court.
it: Work of 3 subcommittees noted
Petitions pending before the court: 1
Entertainment Venues Act B.E. 2509 (1966), Lat Phrao beer-house fire: the Ombudsman reports there is no definition and no specific licence for venues similar to entertainment venues

te: Began studying the fire at a beer venue in Lat Phrao and the Service Establishments Act, and the alleged “phantom father–phantom mother” network falsely claiming nationality rights
se: The meeting closed 3 complaints (a case already decided by the Ombudsman, state property land in Mae Hong Son, and the assessment of flood damage in Pak Phun, Nakhon Si Thammarat) and opened 2 new study topics: gaps in the Entertainment Venues Act B.E. 2509 (1966) after the Lat Phrao beer-house fire, as quite a few shops operate like entertainment venues to avoid zoning; and claims to Thai nationality through the "fake father, fake mother" network.
it: Matters on which the Ombudsman has already issued a decision: 1 / state property land MS.38 of the Mae Hong Son Provincial Administrative Organisation / flood damage assessment, Pak Phun Subdistrict, Nakhon Si Thammarat Province
Results of the work of 3 subcommittees noted

Licensing, supervision and enforcement of the Entertainment Venues Act B.E. 2509 (1966) in the case of the beer-house fire in Lat Phrao (restaurants operating like entertainment venues, avoiding zoning, building inspection)
Preventing wrongful claims to Thai nationality through the "fake father, fake mother" network registering false births, which affects civil registration and security

te: Pushing a development budget for the Suai river basin in Nong Khai, a complaint about cane-based energy in Tak, a village budget in Si Sa Ket, and ride-hailing platforms
se: Follow-up on the development budget for the Suai river basin, Nong Khai Province, which representatives of the committee visited on 25 April 2026; a letter is to be sent to the Governor of Nong Khai asking that the project be included in the provincial development plan. The meeting also considered a complaint from renewable-energy cane farmers in Tak, proposals from a Senators-meet-the-people event in Si Sa Ket, the licence renewal of a ride-hailing platform, and title deeds overlapping public land in Ratchaburi.
it: Pushing a budget to develop the Suai river basin, Nong Khai Province (Lam Nam Suai water source, a bridge over Huai Khu Phrai, floodgates of the Chiang At reservoir); site visited on 25 Apr 2026
Progress of the royally initiated project for the road over the water-supply canal (under consideration by the Ministry of Transport)
A group of farmers growing sugar cane for renewable energy, Tak Province (referred by the Senate agriculture committee)
Senators-meet-the-people, lower north-east: a village subsidy of 1 million baht per village in Kham Niam Subdistrict, and a flood-protection system in Kanthararom Subdistrict, Si Sa Ket
Checking the licence renewal of a ride-hailing platform, and enforcement of the Royal Decree on Digital Platform Services B.E. 2565 (2022) (ETDA's DPS law)
Title deeds overlapping public land and a land allocation licence, Lum Din Subdistrict, Mueang District, Ratchaburi Province

te: Nan land title deeds overlapping public land, housing proposals for Khlong Toei, and damaged roads in Chaiyaphum
se: Nan Province explained that most of the land in Ban Tha Li, Ban Nam Lom and Ban Tha Chang for which title deeds were requested overlaps public land and the Nan River, so deeds cannot be issued. The meeting asked for more information, sent the "Klong Toey Lively Community" proposal to the Senate social development committee and the Port Authority, and wrote to the Governor of Chaiyaphum about repairing the damaged road between Kra Hat and Nong Chim subdistricts.
it: Results of checking title deeds in Ban Tha Li, Ban Nam Lom and Ban Tha Chang, Nan Province: most of the land overlaps public land and the Nan River; 1 plots can receive deeds, and there is a way to prove rights

3 subcommittees: Damrongtham Centres and the central platform / Smart Governance, digital and AI / invited the Department of Public Works and Town & Country Planning and the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation to give information on disasters
Proposal for the "Klong Toey Lively Community" project: allocate 20% of the Port Authority's land for the community (from a Senators-meet-the-people event, lower central region)
Damaged road between Kra Hat and Nong Chim subdistricts, Noen Sa-nga District, Chaiyaphum (referred by the Senate budget monitoring committee)

te: The BMA gave information on the Traffy Fondue system, and complaints from Nan and Phichit were followed up
se: The Permanent Secretary for the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration gave information on the BMA's complaint system, which combines the 1555 hotline, Traffy Fondue, the website and LINE, for the study of a central platform. The meeting wrote to the Director-General of the Department of Lands and the Governor of Nan about title deeds in Mae Sakhon Subdistrict, Wiang Sa District, and to the Governor of Phichit about a complaint on the disciplinary inquiry process concerning a state official, and noted the resignation of Pol.Lt.Gen. Yootana Thaipakdi from the committee.
it: Pol.Lt.Gen. Yootana Thaipakdi resigned as a committee member, effective 18 Jun 2026

Central and Provincial Subcommittee: the Permanent Secretary for the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration gave information on the 1555 complaint system / Traffy Fondue / LINE OA and linking with the central platform
Development Subcommittee (State administration system and public sector personnel): study framework on public services moving to digital government
Complaint asking for land title deeds to be issued faster, Mae Sakhon Subdistrict, Wiang Sa District, Nan
Complaint about the disciplinary inquiry process concerning a state official, Phichit Province
Changes in positions / selection of members to fill vacant seats (secret ballot) / Sakon Nakhon study visit 2–3 Jul / appointment of advisers and subcommittee members

te: A study assigned on making government services more efficient towards a digital civil service, and matters within other committees' remit referred to them
se: The meeting assigned the Subcommittee on the Development of the State Administration System to study making government services more efficient and the move to a digital civil service within 6 months; sent representatives to consider, with the Senate legal affairs committee, the motion "Approaches to solving the problem of colonisation by foreigners who dominate the trade economy and break the law in Thailand" (title as in the motion); referred a complaint about public utilities in Wang Thonglang District to the Senate local government committee; and moved the Sakon Nakhon study visit to 2–3 July 2026.
it: Central and Provincial Subcommittee: 2 vice-chairs of the subcommittee resigned

Development Subcommittee (State administration system and public sector personnel): study on improving the efficiency of public services, digital government and the law on facilitation of licensing consideration (6 months)

Motion "Approaches to solving the problem of colonisation by foreigners who dominate the trade economy and break the law in Thailand" (title as in the motion; under study by the Senate legal affairs committee and tourism committee)
Complaint about a lack of basic utilities on private land, Wang Thonglang District, Bangkok
Study visit on integrated provincial administration, Sakon Nakhon Province
Appointment of 8 honorary advisers, 1 subcommittee members and 1 honorary advisers to subcommittees

te: First meeting under the new chair: a new disaster subcommittee, 10 working groups set up, and a study visit to Sakon Nakhon prepared
se: At the first meeting chaired by Mr. Thawat Surabal, the meeting agreed that the previous disaster subcommittee had completed its term and appointed a new one with 6 months, focusing on reviewing policy, law and warning systems. It noted the resignations of members and advisers, approved 3 persons as committee members, set up 10 working groups, and drafted a programme for a study visit to Sakon Nakhon Province
it: Central and Provincial Subcommittee: progress on the report on Damrongtham Centres and linking the complaint system with the central platform
Disaster Subcommittee: the previous subcommittee completed its mission; a new one was set up with a 6-month study framework (policy, law, warning systems, disaster preparedness)
Resignation of 1 committee member(s) and 1 adviser(s)
Persons as committee members: 3 / draft programme for the Sakon Nakhon study visit, 9–10 Jul 2026 / 10 working groups set up

te: Change of chair: Pol.Lt.Gen. Yootana Thaipakdi resigned, and the meeting elected Mr. Thawat Surabal as the new chair
se: The turning point of the year: Pol.Lt.Gen. Yootana Thaipakdi announced his resignation as chair of the committee, effective 27 May 2026, so the meeting elected Mr. Thawat Surabal as chair under Rule 87, paragraph three. The subcommittees reported that their studies on area-based policy plans, whole-system water management and the effects of the structure of the justice system were complete.
it: Resignations: Pol.Lt.Gen. Yootana Thaipakdi (chair, effective 27 May 2026) / Third Spokesperson of the committee (effective 21 May) / Pol.Maj.Gen. Romsit Weeriyasan (chair of the disaster subcommittee, effective 27 May)
Election of the committee chair to fill the vacancy, under Rule 87, paragraph three, of the Rules of Procedure
Central and Provincial Subcommittee: area-based policy plans (completed) / Damrongtham Centres and the complaint system (being studied)

Development Subcommittee (State administration system and public sector personnel): follow-up on the royally initiated road project over the waterworks canal / complaint about the issuing of land title deeds in Chon Buri Province and the performance of duties by land officials
Disaster Subcommittee: whole-system water management and the effects of the structure of the justice system (completed) / national disaster warning system (being studied)

te: A complaint about public motorcycle-taxi stands sent to the Bangkok Governor, and members appointed to fill 2 vacant seats
se: The meeting resolved to send a complaint about the management of public motorcycle-taxi stands to the Governor of Bangkok to check the facts, and approved the appointment of committee members to fill 2 vacant seats under the Rules of Procedure of the Senate B.E. 2562 (2019).
it: Results of the work of 3 subcommittees noted
Complaint asking for fairness in the management of public motorcycle-taxi stands
Appointment of committee members to fill 2 vacant seats

te: Summary of the committee's key achievements in 5 areas sent to the Senate
se: As the Senate public relations committee asked for key achievements to be selected, the meeting approved 5 works: lessons from the great Hat Yai flood, area-based policy plans, allocation of state land to reduce inequality, the law on facilitating government licensing, and following the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy. It also appointed a working group to study the Kratom Act.
it: Results of the work of 3 subcommittees noted

5 key achievements: (1) lessons from the great Hat Yai flood (disasters) (2) area-based policy plans at every level (security) (3) allocating state land to reduce inequality (society) (4) the licensing facilitation law (society) (5) the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy (economy)
Appointed a working group to study the enforcement of the Kratom Plant Act B.E. 2565 (2022) in Bangkok

te: Summary of the sufficiency-economy event, selection of the committee's key achievements, and a working group set up to study the Kratom Act
se: The meeting approved the report on the sufficiency-economy exhibition and forum held on 27 April 2026, selected the committee's key achievements (Jul 2024 – Apr 2026), such as area-based policy plans, lessons from the great Hat Yai flood, whole-system water management and the licensing facilitation law, and proposed a working group to study the enforcement of the Kratom Act B.E. 2565 (2022) in Bangkok.
it: Summary report of the exhibition and forum "Awakening the Power to Follow the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy" (27 Apr 2026)

Selection of the committee's key achievements, 10 Jul 2024 – 30 Apr 2026: area-based policy plans / lessons from the great Hat Yai flood / whole-system water management / the law on facilitating government licensing
1 subcommittee advisers ended their term
Proposed setting up a working group to study the enforcement of the Kratom Plant Act B.E. 2565 (2022) in Bangkok

te: Experts help frame the seminar "Bangkok 2030–2034: The Next Great Flood", and complaints from Krabi Province
se: The meeting invited Assoc. Prof. Seree Supratid, an expert in water engineering and management, and representatives of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, the Office of the National Water Resources and the Federation of Thai Industries to help frame a seminar on the risk of a great flood in Bangkok in 2030–2034, aimed at policy proposals for a "safe city" and better water-management laws. It also considered 2 complaints.
it: Complaint asking for a check of the disciplinary inquiry process concerning a state official
Complaint about the conduct of executives and officials of a local government organisation, Krabi Province

Discussed the seminar “Bangkok 2030–2034: The Next Great Flood” with Assoc. Prof. Seree Supratid, a water expert, and representatives of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, the Office of the National Water Resources and the Federation of Thai Industries
Proposed appointing advisers to the Subcommittee on Central and Provincial Administration

te: Details of the exhibition and local-wisdom forum "Awakening the Power to Follow the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy" on 27 Apr
se: The meeting noted the programme of the event on 27 April 2026 in the hall in front of the Senate chamber, opened by the President of the Senate, Mr. Mongkol Surasajja, with a living exhibition (sufficiency-living booths, the New Theory of agriculture, sustainable land use) and a forum of local sages, and approved changes to the list of advisers.
it: Results of the work of 3 subcommittees noted

Living exhibition and forum “Awakening the Power to Follow the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy for a Secure and Sustainable Life”, 27 April 2026: the committee chair gave the report, the President of the Senate opened the event; exhibition and local-wisdom forum
3 persons ended their term, and 1 honorary advisers appointed

te: Approved the approach to drafting a law on handling complaints; follow-up on the TOR for textbooks of the Office of the Welfare Promotion Commission for Teachers and Educational Personnel and the Mae Hong Son dialysis centre
se: The meeting approved an approach for drafting a law on complaint handling linked to a central platform overseen by a national committee, will follow up the textbook-printing bidding of the Office of the Welfare Promotion Commission for Teachers and Educational Personnel (OTEP) with the Comptroller General's Department, and will press for the request by the Mae Hong Son Provincial Administrative Organisation to use state property land for a dialysis centre. It also approved a study visit to Nong Pai Kaeo Prison, Chon Buri Province.
it: Central and Provincial Subcommittee: report on area-based policy plans and an approach to drafting a law on handling complaints through a central platform (inviting the DGA, the Office of the Permanent Secretary, Office of the Prime Minister, and the Ministry of Interior to give information, 22 April 2026)

Development Subcommittee (State administration system and public sector personnel): follow-up on the price bidding for printing textbooks 2569 by the Office of the Welfare Promotion Commission for Teachers and Educational Personnel (consistency of the TOR with the invitation announcement), with the Comptroller General's Department
Follow-up on the request to use state property land for a dialysis centre, Mae Hong Son Provincial Administrative Organisation
Study visit on the justice system and preparing inmates before release, Nong Pai Kaeo Prison, Chon Buri
Preparing the exhibition and forum on the Sufficiency Economy, 27 April 2026

te: Study results on Damrongtham Centres, the situation of kratom-drink sales in Bangkok, and preparations for a flood seminar
se: The meeting noted the summary of the Senate Special Affairs Committee meeting, the results of the study on making Damrongtham Centres and the national complaint system more effective, and the review of kratom-drink sales in Bangkok, and discussed preparations for the sufficiency-economy exhibition on 27 April 2026.
it: Summary of the meeting of the Senate Special Affairs Committee No. 3/2569
Central and Provincial Subcommittee: study results on improving the efficiency of Damrongtham Centres and Thailand's petition and complaint systems
Development Subcommittee (State administration system and public sector personnel): the situation of kratom-drink sales in Bangkok
Disaster Subcommittee: preparation for the seminar The Next Great FLOOD, 15 May 2026, Room B1-1
Preparing the exhibition and forum on the Sufficiency Economy, 27 April 2026, in the hall in front of the Senate meeting chamber

te: A complaint about the council of a private university referred to the Senate education committee, and the sufficiency-economy event moved to 27 Apr
se: The meeting considered a complaint about senior personnel management at a private university and resolved to refer it to the Senate education committee, which has direct authority. It approved the approach for the seminar "The Next Great Flood" in room B1-1, and moved the sufficiency-economy exhibition to 27 April 2026.
it: Results of the work of 3 subcommittees noted
Complaint about senior personnel management at the council of a private university (asking the Ministry of Higher Education to check)
Seminar plan for “Bangkok 2030-2034, The Next Great FLOOD”, 15 May 2026, Room B1-1, with speakers invited to a discussion on 29 April 2026
Sufficiency-economy exhibition
Appointment of honorary advisers
